newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - August 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - August 19.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail: biznis@giasdl01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
BRITAIN SEEKS CLARIFICATION ON REMARKS ON QUEEN'S VISIT

The British government has sought a clarification from India on Prime Minister Gujral's remarks on the Queen of England's plan to visit Amritsar in October. Gujral told a London newspaper over the weekend that India had suggested that the Queen drop a visit to Amritsar in view of the sentiments of the Indian people. The Bharatiya Janata Party is saying that an apology from the British for the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in 1919 is long overdue. While in Amritsar, Gurcharan Singh Tohra, president of the body that administers Sikh religious places, condemned the demand for an apology from the Queen saying it was being made by vested interests.
The Economic Times
P & O ASIA ACQUIRES 60.7 PCT STAKE IN JOINT VENTURE

The Great Eastern Shipping has given controlling stake to Dutch tourism major P&O Asia BV in P&O Travel India which is a travel and tourism joint venture. The Great Eastern has reduced its holding to 39.7 percent from 50 percent in 1995. The shareholding of P&O Asia BV has gone up to 60.7 percent. Market sources speculated that the Great Eastern might be trying to get out of the travel and tourism trade, which was in a slump for the last two years. The company owns 40 ships.
CLARION TIES UP WITH BATES

The Clarion Advertising Services announced an affiliation with the $6.3 billion Bates Worldwide, with the Bates planning to pick up stake in the agency in due course. It may pick up a majority stake in Clarion, which is totally owned by the employees. Most of the employees are stated to be willing to transfer their equity shares.
Financial Express
DUFF & PHELPS GIVES INDIA INVESTMENT GRADE

Chicago-based rating major Duff & Phelps Credit Rating assigned a BBB minus investment grade rating to India's foreign exchange obligations. The rating places India at a comfortable position as an investment destination. This rating is equal to the Baa3 rating assigned by the Moodys Investor Services. Duff & Phelps said the investment grading reflected the Indian government's strong policy commitment towards establishing a competitive and creditworthy economy.
FORWARD DOLLAR PREMIA RISE TO 5.83 PCT
The rupee weakened against the forward dollar due to increased demand from the corporates. The sharpest weakening was in the six-month rupee which lost 20 paise on a single day of trading.
Business Standard
GOLD TO BE PUT ON OPEN GENERAL LICENCE LIST

The government will soon place gold on the open general licence list, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) informed the corporates at a meeting recently. At present, special import licences have to be obtained from the Reserve Bank to import gold. These licences are obtained at a premium on a case to case basis. A liberalised gold trade will result in a substantial demand for dollars.
LOCAL FIRMS TOO TO HANDLE GLOBAL DEPOSITORY RECEIPTS

A core group decided that Indian merchant bankers will have to be co-opted and included as members of the syndicate of global bankers handling global depositary receipts offerings of government companies. The decision by a core group of government secretaries is being interpreted as a major boost to the domestic merchant bankers. Indian companies now will have a share in the fees which global managers earn in such deals.
ICI PICKS UP 9.1 PCT STAKE IN ASIAN PAINTS

British Paints group ICI Plc snapped up a 9.1 percent stake in Asian Paints (India) in a two-stage, 1.29 billion rupee deal with Managing Director Atul Choksey and his associates. The deal is subject to clearance by the Foreign Investment Promotion Board.
The Observer
SHARES END LOWER ON THE NATIONAL BOURSE

Share prices drifted lower at the National bourse with participants unwilling to make fresh commitments after a big fall on the Wall Street. The 50-share National bourse index ended 23.95 points (1.9 percent) lower at 1,203.95 provisional close. A holiday at the Bombay bourse too contributed to the sluggish activity.
Business Line
FINANCE FIRMS SEEK INFRASTRUCTURE FINANCE FROM WORLD BANK

The Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) is negotiating with the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank for funds worth about $600 millions to finance infrastructure projects. The Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) is also negotiating with the World Bank for such a facility. Both the proposed lines of credits are expected to be provided at highly competitive rates and for maturities of 20 years.
